verdict.tagline: Costly expansions and jarring era resets overshadow the grand strategy.
for_you_if: you are willing to push past punishing early systems
you want deep historical empire-building campaigns
not_for_you_if: you object to expensive downloadable content models
you cannot stand mechanics that wipe out your progress

single_points.text: One reviewer says the game won't open.

citation.review_text: Well THAT was disappointing! Pre-Ordered Civ VII in 2025, confirmed in March 2026 that I had access to the game (but didn't yet have time to play), and now today finally got around to trying to play the game... and it won't open. Call me old school, but I miss the days when you bought a game and received a physical product; when you buy an online game, you're at the mercy of the internet. This is the LAST time I'll ever buy a video game again. Huge shame, too, as I've been a fan of Civ since the original.

citation.review_text: Couldn't get it to work, got an "Offline Account" error that disabled multiplayer. I tried fixing it for an hour but ended up submitting a refund request.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the unit movement graphic does not update and the end turn failed to work.

citation.review_text: I've played every single Civ game since Civ1  and every iteration gave great improvements. It's always moving forward. What doesn't work is addressed. Well except for this one. The designer removed culture zone (borders), thus allowing other civ to squeeze in between your cities to establish one. Civ3 implemented culture zone to address this but now Civ7 has taken it away. Also, game is extremely buggy. I just started playing, have not gone past 20 turns and I've already encountered several bugs - e.g. you move your unit but the graphic does not update that your unit has moved and the end turn failed to work. So frustrating.

claims.claim: DLC content feels overpriced and cash-grabby on top of an already expensive base game.

citations.review_text: The game is compelling once you learn some of the new mechanics/strategies. I think the addition of leaders and civilizations with their own perks is great, but the starting amount is disappointing and the DLCs really feel like cash grabs on top of an already expensive game.  The DLC bundle didn't feel worth the thirty extra bucks I paid for it. The result is an old civ fan that's been around since the first game disillusioned with the direction of the franchise. Will think much harder before jumping into the next iteration if they continue this DLC squeezing blood from a stone trajectory.
Really overpriced DLC and why on Earth do Assyrian infantry become Indians with turbans in the late game?

After another 10+ hours of play, I’d give the game a passing grade, which means I can offer a very cautious recommendation. That said, I still don’t like the shifting between eras. I also find it quite disappointing that a lot of content is locked behind paid DLC, content that really should have been part of the base game, which costs 70 euros.

If I could, I would cast a neutral vote.

My original review: I’ve spent a great many hours playing Civ 4, 5, and 6. The "just one more turn" feeling is exactly what those games give me. But with the seventh installment, I simply don’t get that so far. I’m not entirely sure why. It certainly looks good (that’s an improvement), but for me the new game mechanics are a real step backward. Maybe I need to give it some more time...

The Worst Civ EVER (I've played the series since Civ 1)

(-) You have Napoleon x2 :D (I could say something here :D)
(-) AGES: Firaxis just killed the CORE of the series, which is playing as one civ without any resets until the atomic annihilation or robotic wipeout of the world.
(-) Crisis near the end of the age. It is a must no matter how great your civ is.
(-) Selection of Slavic countries
(-) Even the Space Age will be locked behind a PAID DLC ...
(-) Money grab: the base game + all DLCs have a horribly insane price.

(+) Nice graphics.
(+/-) They are trying to fix it (but anything that could make this game better is hidden behind an insane paywall).

If you like all prev games in the series, DO NOT BUY this one.

I’ll give this game a chance if the complete edition (with all paid DLCs) ever drops to $20.
The UI makes this game unenjoyable. Too expensive and selling basic stuff that should be in base game as additional content & DLC.

claims.claim: The game has an era transition system that abruptly decimates civilizations, wipes out sponsored city-states, and resets resources.

citations.review_text:
I'm kinda neutral about Civ VII. It has some really good ideas but at the same time fundamental flaws. I think how the era transitions are done is one of the fundamental problems.

The early game is decent. Wars are good, combat is nice, there are plenty of different resources etc. Then comes the era change and it's just brutal. It's a sharp line after which your civilization is decimated. It feels like you're starting a scenario rather than continuing the game. Technology jumps forward a lot, the city states that you sponsored are gone, the luxuries and resources you had allocated to towns are gone. Production is horrible. This whole thing feels very boardgamey. Like in Through the Ages when an era changes, you get a new deck of era cards that are more powerful and you also throw two population out, meaning everything is harder to balance. It works in a boardgame, but not so much in a computer game like Civilization.

The era transitions should be more fluid. It's cool that the game has certain resources unique to each era. And it makes sense that papyrus might be valuable in the ancient times but lose its value as time progresses. I think that should be gradual too. As you invent technologies, it should start a slow decline on old resources while revealing new ones. Other Civilizations finding out improved tech should devalue some of yours if you're far behind. I don't have a good solution to the problem, but the very abrupt era change Civ VII is not it either. It is a very feels-bad moment.

Other thing is the civilization change which, again, makes sense in historic sense, but it's another feel-bad moment that compounds the era change. It can also feel very unthematic to go from Egypt to Vikings. Right now, you can play with your civilization from start to endgame. So, this is kinda fixed. But I'd rather have this work that you can get different bonuses to new era depending on what you did on the current one. The game does suggests civilization changes but shoul…

It's obvious the developers of this 7th game had nothing to do with the game's philosophy. Either this, or they completely lost their minds. The stupidity and the absurdity of the game structure, with ages that reset your progress, leaders with no true origin, migrating from one civ to another for no reason, mechanics that make no sense and a lack of progress and logics, accompanied by the worst soundtrack you could imagine. There is nothing immersive in this mess, everything is artificial, cold and unrealistic. There is no continuity, nothing to attach to, nothing to keep you craving for one more turn. It's that bad that is simply embarrassing. The fact that I bought (with a lot of money) this absurd pathetic attempt to continue what has been done with Civ V and Civ VI feels more of a scam and a total lack of respect for players than a dev failure. I will never buy a Civ game again, ever. I will download every piece of the future releases via torrents, good or bad (most likely bad, I lost faith they still got it), until I will consider myself refunded for this dystopian digital theft. You should be ashamed of yourself.

The Worst Civ EVER (I've played the series since Civ 1)

(-) You have Napoleon x2 :D (I could say something here :D)
(-) AGES: Firaxis just killed the CORE of the series, which is playing as one civ without any resets until the atomic annihilation or robotic wipeout of the world.
(-) Crisis near the end of the age. It is a must no matter how great your civ is.
(-) Selection of Slavic countries
(-) Even the Space Age will be locked behind a PAID DLC ...
(-) Money grab: the base game + all DLCs have a horribly insane price.

(+) Nice graphics.
(+/-) They are trying to fix it (but anything that could make this game better is hidden behind an insane paywall).

If you like all prev games in the series, DO NOT BUY this one.

I’ll give this game a chance if the complete edition (with all paid DLCs) ever drops to $20.

Bad..... with Civ 7 to the franchise is what SimCity (aka SimCity 5) was to city building - dumbed down systems that spat on the franchise.

The whole same Era for whole map with a clock running down and era crisis is such a bad concept; effectively it makes a game a series of 3 mini-games run in sequence.
It really takes away the player agenda to focus on any specific development...

I wanted to give it a chance but can't.
if you are a 4X game fan - avoid.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the 2K account became unlinked from their steam account, removing access to two pieces of DLC and making the game unloadable until fixed.

citation.review_text: It finally hooked me, had a classic marathon session of Civ last night, but then this morning I tried to load the game and couldn't play it because the 2K account became unlinked from my steam account, which removed access to two pieces of dlc, which made the game unloadable. It took 15 minutes to fix. I had to turn the game on and off again several times. All for a DLC that I had already gained access to. If this is their idea for the future of Civ, I'm out. It's sad to see a company like Firaxis, and a game with Sid's name on it, do dumb, short sighted anti-consumer stuff like this.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the AI travels halfway across an empty world to settle a city next to them with no penalties.

citation.review_text:
Just play IV, V, or VI. It's cheaper and just better.

I was so excited for this game. Civ games are one of the few I don't mind DLC or expansions. If I get hundreds of hours out of a game I think it's worth it. I don't mind they changed some mechanics and played around with the progression of the civilizations. I like the idea because that's kind of what happened IRL but what I can't forgive is the AI.

IT RUINED THE GAME FOR ME!

I set it up with one opponent. Made the world huge so I'd get a chance to learn the game before fighting the AI for resources. What does it do? It travels halfway across an empty world to settle a city next to me. No penalties for this. It recommends you do this too. Why? Sure certain civs would want to do this but it's like hard coded into the game that all of them want to do this. If I wanted this experience I would set it up for a small world and go for a domination victory as fast as I could.

Just a silly nitpick is how they animated the weather in the cutscene. Just floating tornadoes with no dark clouds above them. I can't take it seriously and it's actually a joke among the weather community. If you are gonna spend the time and money developing weather for your games at least make it look good. I can forgive the synoptic movement not making sense if it just looked good.

single_points.text: One reviewer says there is poor information and explanations given to the player, making it hard to understand things like trade routes or where negative modifiers come from.

citation.review_text: I have never had such a frustrating time with a 4x game.  there is such poor information and explanations given to the player it is hard to understand where things like why my trade route won't work or where some negative is coming from.  encountered so many bugs and suboptimal design that it actually pissed my group off enough we just dropped our first run through of it completely.  I'd say the game is salvageable, but its been out for over a year and a half at this point...

single_points.text: One reviewer says the tutorials use a lot of words to explain very little and buttons you are directed to click for more information literally do nothing.

citation.review_text:
I preordered this game, but personal issues meant I had to wait over a year after launch to play it. I should never have bothered.

Sid Meier’s Civilization VII has destroyed the series for me. I’ve loved Civ for as long as I can remember, but this game is horrendous.

The more recent editions of Civ added complexity, which I welcomed—even when it made the learning curve steep. Previous games offered clear descriptions and useful tutorials that helped you understand the mechanics. That is far from the case with Civ VII.

Buttons you’re directed to click for more information literally do nothing. The tutorials use a lot of words to explain very little of practical use. You can spend hours reading tooltips and still come away without understanding how things work.

Given the price of the game and its ridiculously overpriced DLC, I expected something enjoyable to play. Instead, I got an exercise in frustration.

Save your money. Beating your head against a brick wall would be a better time than playing this dreck.

I WILL NEVER SUPPORT THIS FRANCHISE OR FIRAXIS GAMES AGAIN!

What's worse is what you get with the DLCs, which is to say, not much: a couple extra leaders, a couple extra civilizations. Eh? single_points.text: One reviewer says the loading screens were ghastly and the game felt bare bones and half baked.

citation.review_text:
So… this is one of the most difficult reviews I have ever had to give. I am enormous Civilization fan and I am extremely extremely easy to satisfy. I have played Paradox games and paid paradox prices and been happy as a clam. This games release and the last year or so of management has been extraordinarily disappointing. 

I was extremely hyped for this game. The leaders? Sick as hell. The civs, also cool. The art style, the narrator, the bold new vision, all seemed really interesting and cool! And then the game came out. The art style of the game itself was good but in a lot of other places it felt soulless, particularly the loading screens just were ghastly. The game felt so bare bones and half baked. You couldn’t even play “Just One More Turn”. It felt like a Civ game had been released for beta testing. 

Then the DLCs and expansion packs started coming out immediately and it left such a bad taste in my mouth. The expansions do not add nearly enough for the price they are asking for. If there were twice as many leaders and wonders and new mechanics or whatever, I’d be fine with it. Once again, I play paradox games, I’m no stranger to an expansion pack that costs too much money but at least (oftentimes) it’s worth it to get to add something new to the game. I cannot really say the same here. 

I am an extremely forgiving player and am more than willing to give the benefit of the doubt and take into consideration things like the cost of production, inflation, and whatever other factors have driven some of these decisions, but as of right now, I can’t recommend this game. The game is still not in a state that feels finished. It’s still lacking basic mechanics. Expansion packs don’t make up for it. The DLCs may be make it or break it for this game honestly and even then, the DLCS may not be able to wash out the bad taste in my mouth of a game being released half baked and then selling basic aspects of a game under the guise of add ons. 

I feel really bad leaving suc…

single_points.text: One reviewer says there are silly UI issues like having to click on the unit needs orders all day instead of directly skipping to the next unit.

citation.review_text:
I bought the game at release in an unplayable state. Now it is a really solid game. You can argue about whether you like the new mechanics or not, but it finally feels like a CIV game, imo.

However it has quite a few silly UI issues and annoyances (ranging from mild to PLEASE GOD, CAN YOU PLEASE DIRECTLY SKIP TO THE NEXT UNIT INSTEAD OF MAKING ME CLICK ON THE "UNIT NEEDS ORDERS" ALL DAY PLEASSSEEEEEE). In my opinion, it's unacceptable to take steps backwards in something as basic as UI design and quality-of-life features.

All in all, 8/10, would recommend. Hope it gets fully polished in the near future.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the domination victory condition was changed so major powers never need to go to war with each other, and you can't deconstruct or relocate an existing building.

citation.review_text:
What the hell do you MEAN you changed the domination victory condition? It has always been that you need to conquer every capital city, and now it's changed so that the major powers never even need to go to war with each other? Horrible, terrible fumble. 

Other than my current anger at that particular change, the pros/cons of this civ title are genuinely mixed. The gameplay is very good, planning cities is MOSTLY very good except that you can't deconstruct/relocate an existing building, the city state/barbarian system is excellent. Diplomacy is... mostly good. I hate that I can't trade cities in the diplomacy screen anymore. 

The major problem is the game's signature new feature, the age transitions. It's way better than it was at launch, not nearly as disruptive, but I still don't like it. Civ has always been about the march of a nation through time, balancing the aspects of your empire to dominate the board in whatever way you see fit. Guiding your nation from single village to space-age superpower. This new mechanic injects unwelcome gamey-ness into that fantasy, it forcibly reminds you that you're playing a game, and that it's approaching midnight and you really _shouldn't_ play "just one more turn."

Despite all that I've been enjoying it, but the biggest reason of all that this review lands solidly in a "do not recommend" category is the inexcusable greed of the publisher and developer. This game launched with massive holes in its civ and leader roster, which were available at launch with an incredible expensive expansion pass. Locking Britain behind a paywall is just... your greed sickens me, and I refuse to reward this behavior any further than I already have with the game purchase.

The UI gets in the way of simple basic game play, It  acts like every new start is a players first time.  And then they changed the entire flow of the game.  It's not fun anymore. single_points.text: One reviewer says it is impossible to track city state Suzerain and Befriending status and religion identification in the exploration age relies on a tiny icon.

citation.review_text: Not good, game gets boring after the antiquity age, and a lot of UI quality of life things in Civ 6 are gone. It's impossible to track city state Suzerain and Befriending status, unlike in Civ 6 where they had a page for it. If you're doing religion in the exploration age you have to identify religions by a tiny icon located on its name bar, and if you're looking at your general production of say gold, the page for that will list what each city is producing, but then they have "Other Sources" part and it's producing half my gold, which doesn't help me identify if it's through trade routes or policies. Plus everything in this game is poorly described, nothing tells you factory resources apply empire wide. It's a game where you have to play with google open just to make sure you're playing it right. Also they're selling civilization DLCs for the price of Gathering Storm, which is just ridiculous. Who is paying $30 for 6 civilizations you could just mod in. I will say I like the city/town system, and crises/events at the end of ages.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the user interface is awful and nothing tells you how the ruleset will work in practice.

citation.review_text:
I have logged 10s of thousands of hours playing each and every Civ game since Civ 1. I have over 6,000 hours of playing Civ 6. I have cherished all of these games.

This is the first Civ title that I would not  only recommend I would actively campaign that nobody buys or plays. it is simply, awful and unplayable. 

it will take a complete re-write to be playable and a completely different development team. it has no subtlety, the user interface is just awful, the game has been simplified to the level that it is just monotonous and frustrating. 

As a player you have no idea how the ruleset will work in practice and so there is no point in learning the rules. Just utterly unplayable and awful.

I dearly hope sales are rock bottom so that Faraxis have no choice but to sack everybody involved in its development for the next Civ in 5 years time.

single_points.text: One reviewer says there is no distinction between light or heavy cavalry units and diplomacy and spying are simplified.

citation.review_text:
This game caters to the gen z that's afflicted by tiktok-brainrot.

You can't compare civ 7 to civ 5 or 6 it's just to different very few similarities to simplistic.

The  antiquity mixes in the bronze age with early medieval period, there is no distinguish between light or heavy cavalry units. The exploration age goes from early medieval period until just around 1700. I can't speak for the modern age because I won a culture victory in the late stages of the exploration age.

To make this a better game it should have had far more distinct and broken down ages, and not been so bloody simple. Civ 5-6 made unit distinguishes where archer was great against spearmen, cavalry was great for archers, and spearmen where great for cavalry. Here I do not see these values, or they may simply be hidden.

The diplomacy mechanic and spying also simplified.

I do like the crisis mechanic yet it's also simplified, I don't mind the age transitions but it's once again to unrefined.

My conclusion is firaxis has catered to gen z and forgotten the core players that love and cherish civ since first release in the early 90's.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the game forces the screen to go to the town for upgrades even if you don't have money.

citation.review_text: I have played 63 hours in the game so far and I also own the Civ 6 complete with DLCs and I must say this new game is totally different from the last one and I find the game mechanics much more complicated to understand and this new ages mechanic where you lose progress and kind of start over with some progress is a big pain. I like the new commander feature for troops but also a not so easy to use. The game has nice visuals but I feel it is a little complicated to understand compared to the last game and I feel you get a lot less in return for the investment as the game is very very expensive and I don't think I would buy add ons for this and spend the money as the base game hasn't captured my attention yet as something I want to play all the time. The learning of the game is hard and tiring. I don't like the spy mechanics in the new game either.  I don't agree with the settlement cap feature and also now only the first settlement is a city and after that your settlers create towns which you need to buy the upgrade to cities which is like Humankind. The new game are going this route of city cap and I don't  agree as the focus is for you to expand but they limit you to this feature as going over the city cap your happiness is penalised. Once playing the games and there are town upgrades to be done the game forces the screen to go the town for upgrades even if you don't have money to upgrade and the force screen thing is a pain to play the game as it has so many mechanics which is way to complicated if you just want to relax. Uprading your town eventually kind of gets capped and then you get specialisation which you lose with because it in many cases loses you happiness and costs money with only sometime giving you added science or culture. The buffs for this game in science and culture as not as good as in Civ 6 I think. The feature of ages now is very different and for example when changing ages you loose progress in a city state and your cities could go back to be…

single_points.text: One reviewer says the map becomes an informational mess and a strain on the eyes by the Modern era and historical factions lack asymmetry with copied assets.

citation.review_text:
The main issue I have with this is I don’t know what I’m doing and nothing is explained very well in-game. 

Once you get to the Exploration age, everything just becomes an informational mess. 

I never had this issue with Civ 6 or Civ 5 when I played them (albeit not a great deal either). 

They really need to clean it up if they want to expand into the Atomic/Information age as by the Modern era, the map is a horrible mess and a strain on the eyes. 

Also, the DLC is so half-baked. 

Bulgarians using Arab swordsman, Sengoku Japan using Mongolian archers, Carthage just looking the same as the Greeks. 

What drew me to Civ 7 before release was the asymmetry of the factions. They have given up on this now and just copy and paste half the assets from over Civs. 

I mean, Mongolian archers fighting for Sengoku Japan? Why can’t they just use the same model as Heian Japan anrchers? Also Samurai cavalry with shields. So much for historical flavour.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the world map is too graphically busy, causing over-stimulation and making it difficult to find units and cities.

citation.review_text:
I can't finish a full game nor feel enticed to want to play it regularly. I have been trying to figure out why that is and why I'm so drawn towards the games from the total war series. I think I've narrowed it down to two issues. 

My first issue is that the world/map is too graphically busy for me. I can't easily see and find things like my units easily. I think I'm straight up over stimulated. When I zoom out I want to get a lay for the land, but all I see is 'stuff' everywhere. I can't be bothered to use map filters- I use those when I'm in an analytics mood. I want to see my cities and my units easily and I'm visually impaired from doing so. I think this is why I spent ages playing and loving Civ 3. 

My second issue is that there are too many toil-based activities in the game for me. It honestly feels like my day job trying to figure out out where to place tiles and all the mechanics nowadays that go into it. To be honest, I don't really care for this level of detail in a Civ game. If I want that level of detail, I'd play Skylines.

I don't know. I just can't pretend I'm this benevolent ruler that crushes the insidious despots of the world. I'm too busy finding my units, assaulted by sprawling city graphics and busyness everywhere, and mired down in the muck and toil of tile placement and futile attempts to get them perfect.

single_points.text: One reviewer says multiplayer is ruined by an 8-civilization limit which leaves only 6 AI opponents on a small map.

citation.review_text: The game is great in single-player, but multiplayer is ruined by the 8-civilization limit. If you want to play with a friend, you're left with a maximum of 6 AI opponents, and even a small map feels empty.

single_points.text: One reviewer says city limits ruin the game because exceeding them causes all production to plummet.

citation.review_text: I've been playing every Civ game since Civ II. Civ VII is very disappointing.  I waited over a year to buy it based on reviews hoping it would get better.  Its just not fun, the city limits ruin the traditional take of the world mentality.  You have endless turns of not being able to do anything because you're city limit is over exceeded and all production plummets.  It makes the game so boring.   The ages and civilization changes just make no sense.  This is the first review I've ever left of anything because I can't stand seeing something I've loved for 3 decades be ruined by trying to copy other games that missed the mark.  I'm extremely disappointed.
